title: Colonialism Phase Of Mercantilism
definition: The first phase of British colonialism in India (approx. 1757-1813), characterized by a monopoly of trade, direct plunder of Indian wealth, and the forced purchase of Indian manufactured goods using revenues extracted directly from India.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for understanding the transition of the East India Company from a trading corporation to a territorial sovereign power, explaining the 'Drain of Wealth', and forming the foundation of modern economic history questions in both Prelims and Mains (GS Paper I).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Colonialism Phase Of Mercantilism.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Carnatic Wars and Battle of Plassey (1757)
